And that's not their fault — it's because the equation got handed to them without the story behind it.\n\nSo here's the story. Imagine you're walking along a straight path on a hillside. The ratio of those two changes, delta y divided by delta x, tells you how steep your path is and which direction it tilts. That ratio is m, the slope. Notice I said ratio — it's not just how big the numbers are, it's how they relate to each other.\n\nAnd b? That's even simpler. It's just asking: when x is zero — when you're standing right at the starting post — how high up are you? That height is b, the y-intercept.\n\nHere's what I want you to hold onto as we go through this lesson: m and b are independent. Changing one doesn't force the other to change. That independence is actually the whole power of the equation. We're going to watch what happens on a real graph when we tweak m, then tweak b, and you're going to predict what happens before I show you.
